title: Bayesian Chirp Sampler for Per-Shard Kernel Selection & Amortized Microbench Caching
creator: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: Runtime kernel choice currently relies on static heuristics and occasional probe bursts that are expensive at scale or slow to adapt for per-shard behavior (tenant/region/model/seq-len). This ticket implements a lightweight online sampler — the 'Bayesian Chirp Sampler' — that issues short, chirped microbenchmarks across candidate kernels per shard, builds a per-shard posterior over latency and cost, and caches amortized microbench results to avoid repeated probing. Goals: 1) reduce 99th-pct tail latency regression from wrong kernel picks, 2) minimize probe overhead (<= 0.5% of request QPS amortized), 3) adapt to changing seq-len distributions within 1 minute, 4) provide confidence intervals and a fallback safety policy for strict SLO routes. Success criteria: A) End-to-end 99th-pct latency reduction of >10% on mixed workloads in canary; B) Probe overhead <= 0.5% CPU/GPU time in steady-state for Dedicated clusters; C) No increase in error rate or memory growth over 72h test; D) Feature gated and rolloutable by route/model. Design summary: - Per-shard probe budget is proportional to the shard's QPS and variance in seq-len. - The sampler issues a chirp: a sequence of microbenchmarks with increasing sequence lengths (e.g., 8, 32, 128) to quickly learn kernel performance surface as a function of length. - Use a lightweight Bayesian bandit (Gaussian process with simple kernel or Thompson sampling on normal posterior) to estimate latency/cost tradeoff and uncertainty. - Cache microbench outcomes keyed by (arch-fingerprint, kernel-id, seqlen-bucket, quantization-profile) with TTL and amortized cost accounting. - Use confidence-aware routing: only switch primary kernel when posterior shows >2x improvement in expected latency-cost with low variance; otherwise prefer conservative choice. - Safety: route-level override if tail latency crosses alert thresholds; async re-probing and warm-start from catalog. Implementation plan: 1) Prototype sampler service and microbench harness in runtime -> spike (2w). 2) Integrate sampler with runtime kernel picker API, add cache layer and TTL semantics (1w). 3) Offline simulation using historical trace sampling to tune priors and chirp schedules (1w). 4) Canary on a low-traffic shard, measure overhead and SLOs, iterate (2w). 5) Gradual rollout with observability and feature flag (2w). Trade-offs and considerations: - Complexity vs benefit: Bayesian model adds code and maintenance; mitigated by simple model and strong unit tests. - Probe cost vs adaptivity: chirped probes give broad coverage with few runs; TTL and amortization reduce repeated costs. - Cold-start: use catalog priors and nearest-architecture warm-starts to avoid heavy probing on very low-QPS shards. - Safety-first: conservative thresholds prevent oscillation and flapping. Observability and telemetry: - New dashboards: per-shard kernel posterior heatmap, probe rate, probe latency distribution, cache hit ratio, rollout status. - Tracing: label probe requests and record kernel-choice-decisions. - Alerts: probe-overhead >1% or route-level 99th-pct regressions. Rollout strategy: feature-flag default off -> enable for dedicated-dev cluster -> enable for opt-in customers -> broad rollout for Dedicated after 4-week validation. Links: design doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Bayesian+Chirp+Sampler; spike notebook https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/chs-sampler-spike; dashboard (canary) https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd1234/kernel-sampler-canary; initial PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6573
comments: 2026-02-21 | Avery Chen: Kickoff notes and scope defined. Decided to keep the Bayesian model intentionally lightweight (analytic posterior) to avoid heavy dependency on full GP libs.
2026-02-26 | Marco Alvarez: Completed microbench harness spike. Found that single-shot microbench variance at seqlen=128 is ~12% on p4d. Will use 4-sample chirps to reduce variance; updated design.
2026-03-02 | Priya Nair (SRE): Recommended adding a per-shard probe-rate hard cap to prevent noisy tenants from causing cluster-wide overhead. Added to plan.
2026-03-06 | Marco Alvarez: Implemented cache layer with TTL 6h default. Observed initial cache hit ratio ~82% on the canary shard after 24h.

2026-03-10 | QA (Jon Park): Running 72h soak. No memory leaks. 99th-pct latency improved ~11% for canary model but probe overhead measured 0.7%—needs tuning to meet target. Lowering chirp frequency and increasing amortization reduces overhead to 0.35% in experiment #3.
2026-03-14 | Product (Lena Ortiz): Reviewed canary metrics; requested a short doc for operators describing rollout toggles and how to troubleshoot flapping kernel switches.
2026-03-14 | Marco Alvarez: Updated PR with operator runbook and feature flag gating. Preparing for Dedicated dev cluster expansion next week.
